rawCandidates.title: Meridial – Senior Research Software Engineer – Image Processing
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
About Meridial

Meridial is a Focused Research Organisation (FRO) with a mission to bring connectomics into the living brain. We are building a platform for longitudinal, synapse-resolution mapping of functional neural circuitry in preclinical models. Our aim is to deploy this platform for translational projects and improve drug development outcomes for disorders of the central nervous system.

Meridial is a new not-for-profit FRO in the Convergent Research Ecosystem and funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA).

The technical challenge

Our imaging platform records the activity of neurons and synapses in the living brain. The scientific value of these recordings depends on converting raw images into reliable, quantitative data.

This is a demanding image processing problem. Fluorescence signals are faint, noisy and spatially overlapping; residual tissue motion and other imaging artefacts must be corrected; in addition to conventional planar frames, data may be acquired from arbitrarily shaped 3D regions or several depths at once; properties vary between signal types and experimental configurations; and the same cells and synapses must be reliably matched across imaging sessions spanning weeks. You will build a software package that addresses these challenges in two modes: real-time processing and visualisation, with latencies of tens to hundreds of milliseconds, that inform experimental decisions at the microscope, and offline pipelines that deliver maximum accuracy for scientific analysis and serve as the benchmark for the real-time methods.

The impact of this work is direct and visible: your software will be used at the microscope as experiments unfold, and your pipelines will generate the data underpinning new insights into how neural circuits function and how they change in disease.


Key responsibilities

You will own Meridial’s image processing software end to end, starting from the interface with microscope control and acquisition all the way to processed results prepared for biological analysis. This is a role with a high degree of autonomy: you will make the main design and technology decisions, set priorities with the people who use the software, and work out what to build as requirements emerge.

Who you will work with

  • Experimental team. The neuroscientists running experiments are the main users of the real-time tools. You will work with them at the microscope, understand their problems and turn joint solutions into reliable tools.
  • Senior Software Engineer. Develops the microscope control and image acquisition software, mostly in Rust. Your real-time code exchanges data with that software but need not be part of it. Together, you will decide how the two systems connect.
  • Neuroscience Data Scientist. Owns Meridial’s database and the downstream scientific analysis. You will ensure processed results reach the database with a full record of how they were produced.
  • Reporting line. You will join the Computational Team and report to its Head once appointed, and to the Director of Experimental Research until then.

    • What you will do

  • Build robust pipelines for motion and artefact correction, segmentation of cells and synapses, separation of overlapping signals and extraction of activity over time, adapted to different signal types.
  • Register data from flexible 3D imaging modes to reference volumes, and build tools that find the same field of view and match cells and synapses across sessions, both live at the microscope and offline at high resolution.
  • Develop real-time versions of these methods that keep up with streaming data, including fast identification of cells as stimulation targets.
  • Build live visualisations and summary measures, such as rolling averages, response histograms and noise metrics, that help scientists steer experiments.
  • Define, with the Senior Software Engineer, the interface between acquisition and processing, with a focus on throughput and low latency.
  • Evaluate and adapt existing open-source tools, develop new methods where needed, and validate them against ground truth, using offline results as the benchmark for the real-time processing.
  • Optimise for speed and scale, using multi-threading, GPUs or compiled languages where needed, so that processing keeps up with large and growing datasets.
  • Write clean, tested and documented code, and set up version control, continuous integration and documentation practices for the codebase.
  • Use AI coding assistants to work efficiently, while keeping code correct and maintainable.
  • Plan and track work in Jira or another project management system, in short iterations with the experimental team.
  • Turn prototypes into reproducible tools that scientists can use and that can be released as open source.

    • The person we are looking for

    You are an experienced software engineer with a background in image analysis or computer vision. You enjoy hard technical problems and set high standards for correctness, performance and code quality. You like working directly with the people who use your software: understanding their problems, trying out ideas with them and turning the best into reliable tools.

    You enjoy building from scratch and are comfortable with the ambiguity of an early-stage organisation. As the main developer of our image processing software, you will work independently and shape how it evolves.

    Experience in any of these areas would help you hit the ground running, but none is required: real-time or streaming data processing, microscopy or scientific image analysis, statistics, or machine learning for image analysis. A background in biology, biophysics or neuroscience would also help.


    Essential experience
  • Experience with image analysis or computer vision, such as segmentation, motion correction, registration or denoising, including image quality measures like signal-to-noise ratio.
  • 5+ years of software development experience, in industry or research (for example, PhD or postdoctoral work where software was a main output).
  • Strong proficiency in Python, with good engineering practice: Git, automated testing and well-documented code.
  • Experience with performance optimisation, such as multi-threading or GPU programming, and with a compiled language such as C/C++ or Rust (if not Rust, a willingness to learn it).
  • Experience building interactive, high-performance data visualisations.
  • Experience building data-intensive pipelines for large datasets, from requirements through to deployment.
  • Experience working directly with end users who are not developers, gathering requirements and turning feedback into improvements.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants in your day-to-day development.

    • Physical demands
  • Fine motor skills for operating computers and office/lab equipment
  • Ability to move light-to-moderately heavy items (typical lab supplies/equipment); may include occasional lifting/carrying with appropriate equipment (e.g., carts/dollies)

    • Position type / schedule
  • Start date: February 2027 or later.
  • Full-time.
  • Based in London, with an on-site presence of four days per week.

    • Additional information
  • Please send your CV.
  • We will ask for two references during the interview process.
  • Generous benefits will be communicated during interviews.
  • For exceptional candidates, Meridial will consider visa sponsorship and relocation support.

    • We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and do not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law or company policy. We strive for a diverse, healthy and safe workplace and strictly prohibit harassment of any kind.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Founding Product Manager - Claap
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
we're hiring our first PM at Claap. You'll own the core product across three big topics in-app agentic experience, off-app agentic experience and enterprise readiness working directly with Robin, our co-founder and CEO.

About Claap

Claap is the AI-native Revenue Intelligence platform for sales and revenue teams.

What makes us different: we were the first platform in our category designed from day one to be used by both humans AND AI agents. We were also the first in our category to release an MCP, back in May 2025, over 18 months ago. Every customer conversation we capture is structured for two consumers: the rep who needs to act on it, and the agents (yours, ours, third-party) that need to feed on it to do their work.

This matters because the biggest shift we see across our customer base, from Series B startups to enterprise customers like Infopro Digital, Didomi, Dash0, and Pelico, is the move toward collaboration between humans, agents, and software. Our customers' executives are under real pressure to deploy AI across sales, business development, and customer-facing functions. Claap is often the conversation-data backbone that makes those agentic workflows possible.

Claap is now part of lempire (lemlist), giving us the ambition to build the agentic revenue platform (from prospection to closing) of the next decade.

We're a small team. Every hire matters and we are looking for our 1st PM.

As the first Product Manager at Claap, your mission is to drive the product's future developments and roadmap, working hand in hand with Robin, our co-founder and CEO, who has led product since day one.

You will work with Robin on three big topics:

- In-app agentic experience: In the past few months, we have extended our context infra. We now need to put this context at work to truly move the needle for our sales clients and help them close faster. Think next best action for the sales rep (prep meeting, build decks, contact people, follow ups & co), assisted pipeline reviews & forecasts or sales coaching.

- Off-app agentic experience: Claap is becoming headless, consumed more and more through MCP. We now need to level up our MCP integrations to make Claap fully sticky and efficient through MCP usage in 3rd party agents. Think MCP tools, plugins, embed skills or Claude artifact app.

- Enterprise readiness: our customers are moving upmarket, and enterprise accounts need governance, admin settings, permissions and configuration capabilities to roll Claap out at scale. Think SSO/SCIM, roles and permissions, data retention policies, and admin analytics.

The lemlist integration and our end-to-end sales agent roadmap will stay with Robin, which leaves you real ownership on the core Claap product (ie closing).

Your role is to understand the market and customer needs (especially in this AI era), identify the best possible product evolutions, prioritize them, work hand-in-hand with developers and designers to build an amazing product experience, and have a strong focus on go-to-market with Sales and Marketing to make sure the impact is reached.

Your scope can change over time; we are a truly agile company: we iterate a lot, even on how we organize and work together.

The PM at Claap wears different hats

- A detective/explorer hat to find unusual insights & opportunities, read between the lines of what sales teams really need, and be visionary when needed

- A chess player hat to think strategically, create good decision constraints, double down on the right things, and always have a coup d'avance

- An investor hat to make the right bets at the right time with the right amount of resources, because you sometimes need to play fast and risky, and sometimes need to play safe

- A diplomat hat to influence your teammates on what we should spend time and effort on, win their trust, and bring visibility, focus, vision and motivation

- A builder hat to get your hands dirty with AI, prototype, test and ship, instead of only writing specs about it

What you are not

- A Project Manager who only talks about methodologies and frameworks

- A Product Owner writing super detailed 4-page tickets for devs

- A feature factory building every custom request an enterprise prospect asks for

- The "Notion docs & meetings person" with no real impact on our users and the business

- A "yes man" for every idea and suggestion people bring to you

- A people manager looking for a team to run: this role is hands-on

Key results

Within 3 months you will have

- Developed a deep understanding of Claap, the call intelligence market and our product vision

- Built relationships with Claap users, from sales reps to the admins of our largest accounts

- Mapped the enterprise requirements that slow down or block our deals, and shipped the first ones

- Identified the key closing jobs to be done and shipped first iterations with your squad

- Won the trust of your squad, Robin, and the Sales and CS teams

Within 12 months you will have

- Made Claap truly enterprise-ready: governance, settings and configuration are no longer a reason we lose a deal

- Made Claap a must-have in our users' closing workflow, with measurable adoption and retention

- Positively impacted the company's revenue through solutions you've helped launch

- Influenced the Claap product vision by suggesting transformative developments

What's in it for you?

- A founding role: you're the first PM at Claap, with real ownership on a fast-growing AI product and a direct line to the founders

- Helping thousands of sales professionals close more deals

- A chance to work with an innovative, fast-paced team with a bias for action

- Opportunity to shape our company's direction

- Potential to establish yourself as an expert in AI for sales

Preferred experience

Must have

- You have 5+ years of experience in product. Scale-up experience is highly preferred.

- You have a strong academic background (business school, engineering school or equivalent) and/or experience in top-tier companies.

- You are a hands-on PM: you are an individual contributor today, or you led product at an early-stage startup.

- You have a real taste and curiosity for AI and tech, ideally with features or agents you've launched end to end.

- You have a big bias for action: you are a "débrouillard" and understand the value of speed & execution.

- You have strong communication skills.

- You speak French and English. This is non-negotiable: most of our enterprise accounts are French-speaking.

- You have a strong pragmatism.

- You have a solid knowledge of SaaS markets & mechanisms.

- You have a strong business acumen.

Nice to have

- You have experience in enterprise or upper mid-market SaaS (permissions, admin, SSO, security reviews).

- You have worked on sales tech, revenue intelligence or tools used by sales teams.

- You have Growth, Revenue Operations or Sales experience.

- You know how to wireframe designs.

- You are humble and look for clues that you are wrong.

- You are curious, always asking questions and learning new stuff.

Additional Information

- Competitive salary + profit sharing

- Where you live and work is totally up to you: we do have an office in Paris if you enjoy life at the office 🇫🇷

- Profit sharing: when lempire wins, all team members share the profits

- Alan Blue: comprehensive 100% premium medical coverage for you and your family

- Swile Meal Tickets: daily meal tickets to fuel productivity

- Navigo Card: 100% covered Navigo card

- Full-remote work setup: a well-funded home office budget

- Gear: a laptop + the tools and equipment you need for your job

- Team building: we all meet once a year at really cool places around the world

Recruitment process

- Interview with Victoire, our Talent Acquisition Manager

- Interview with Robin, Claap co-founder and CEO

- Business Case (async.) + Live Q&A with Robin and Pierre

- Team fit

- Interview with Charles, our CEO

- Reference Check

- Offer

How to apply

Include a short note (200 words max) on an AI feature or agent you shipped end to end. It's the hardest thing to read on a CV, so we screen for it from day one.

rawCandidates.title: Lead Customer Success
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
At Parallel, we build AI agents that help healthcare organizations automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.

Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost to manual, repetitive administrative tasks. Legacy software hasn't helped: it has made work slower, more complex and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change this. Our technology combines large language models with system-level automation to do real work inside existing hospital tools. No integration, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding and frees up time for medical teams to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024 and already have 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people. We are backed by top-tier investors (Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI), and this is just the beginning.

The future of healthcare isn't just digital, it's automated. Come help us build it!

The role

Context

This new role comes as our customer base grows rapidly, driven in particular by deployments in private healthcare facilities. Its purpose is to ensure our customers get the most out of our solution and are fully satisfied with it.

As Lead Customer Success, you will own customer usage and satisfaction, and manage our Customer Support team of two experienced people. This is a hands-on Lead role: you will manage the team while still spending a significant share of your time working directly on accounts. You will work closely with Clémentine (Head of Ops), the Deployment Strategists, the Product team, and RevOps.

Missions

  • Account monitoring: track usage metrics for each hospital and define the indicators to watch.

  • Detection and resolution: spot accounts in trouble (for example a hospital whose activity suddenly drops), raise the alarm and solve the issue, on your own or with the Deployment Strategists.

  • Satisfaction: set up and follow NPS campaigns.

  • Adoption: run campaigns to increase usage of Parallel across our customers.

  • Product feedback: share what you see in the field and work with Product on levers to increase usage.

  • Management: manage two experienced people, set the framework and priorities, help them grow and structure the team as the number of accounts increases.

Who you are

  • You have 3 to 5 years of experience in Customer Success, with your own B2B customer portfolio.

  • You have already managed people, even an intern, and you have the credibility to lead two experienced people.

  • You have already set up NPS campaigns and done account monitoring: you know which indicators you track and how you detect an account in trouble.

  • You make decisions on your own on an account and raise the alarm when a metric drops.

  • You want to keep working directly on accounts on top of managing: this is not a pure management role.

  • A plus: experience with key account portfolios.

Our values

  • Play to Win: we're not here to just take part, deliver something "good enough" or simply enjoy the startup ride. We want to win. That means caring about results, moving fast and bringing the right intensity when it matters.

  • High Trust, High Standards: trust is our starting point. If you join us, it's because we believe you can own your scope and make good decisions. We don't want a company built on approvals, control and micromanagement. But trust comes with accountability: the more freedom you have, the higher the bar.

  • Low Ego, Hands-On: at Parallel, no one is above the work. No title, seniority or past success exempts anyone from getting involved in the actual work. Leading means taking responsibility, not distancing yourself from execution.

  • Don't Take Yourself Too Seriously: we take our mission very seriously, not ourselves. Building a company is intense. We want Parallel to remain a place where people enjoy spending time together, laughing, celebrating and giving energy to others. High standards and a good atmosphere aren't opposites: we want both.

Hiring process

  1. Call with the Hiring Team (30 min)

  2. Call with Clémentine, Head of Ops and your future manager (30 min)

  3. An afternoon at our office to present your case and meet the founders (2 hours)

  4. Reference check

Why join us?

  • A role to build: you lay the foundations of customer success at Parallel (metrics, campaigns, team organisation).

  • A key role: customer success weighs heavily on Parallel's reputation, and you are the right hand of the Head of Ops on this topic.

  • Real traction: seed and Series A ($20M with Index Ventures) closed in less than a year, more than 800 clients and a team of over 30 people.

  • Strong investors and founders: Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI; founders who come from Meta, McKinsey and Hublo.

  • A complete package: competitive salary and BSPCE, Alan health insurance, Swile meal vouchers, Apple equipment, 50% of public transport covered.

  • The team: a team event every month and two offsites a year.

  • Our office: Paris 2nd arrondissement.

  • Flexibility: on average one remote day per week and one remote week per year.

 
 
 

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.
If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

À propos de Lexroom

Chez Lexroom, nous développons l'état de l'art de la recherche juridique agentique. Chaque source est minutieusement analysée, les liens implicites entre principes sont identifiés, et toutes les informations sont synthétisées dans un rapport structuré, avec chaque affirmation soigneusement sourcée. Ce qui, auparavant, demandait une semaine à une équipe se réalise désormais pendant une pause café.

Notre mission : rendre le droit plus rapide, plus clair et plus fiable, afin que les avocats et les directions juridiques puissent se concentrer sur l'essentiel.

Nous construisons l'équipe commerciale en France, et nous cherchons la personne qui va la former, l'accompagner et la faire monter en compétence à travers la Lexroom Sales Academy.

  • Un marché en pleine effervescence : tous les cabinets français recherchent une solution IA, et les usages sont encore à inventer.

  • Un avantage concurrentiel fort : vous ne formez pas des commerciaux à vendre un assistant IA de plus, mais une approche radicalement nouvelle que les prospects n'ont jamais vue.

LA MAISON JACQUEMUS
 
Jacquemus a été fondée par Simon Porte Jacquemus en 2009 à Paris, en France.
Dédiée à la mémoire de la mère du créateur, la marque puise son inspiration dans une passion pour la culture. Les collections femme et homme font référence à l'art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture.
 
Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. Plus récemment, la marque a investi des lieux tels que le canal du Château de Versailles (Le Chouchou), la Fondation Maeght (Les Sculptures), la Casa Malaparte (La Casa) et l'appartement parisien d'Auguste Perret (La Croisière).
 
Basé dans le 8ᵉ arrondissement de Paris, Jacquemus est une maison de mode indépendante comptant plus de 300 employés. Réputée pour sa forte présence numérique et son expansion internationale, la marque a développé des expériences de vente innovantes à travers le monde avant d'ouvrir son premier flagship permanent au 58 Avenue Montaigne à Paris en 2022. Depuis, des boutiques ont été ouvertes à New York (SoHo) et Londres (New Bond Street).
 
 
 
VOTRE ROLE

Rattaché(e) à la Head of Design, vous intervenez sur la création des collections homme et femme, jersey, bain et flou show, des recherches d'images jusqu'au suivi des prototypes en normalisation.

VOTRE PROFIL

Vous justifiez d'une première expérience d'environ 2 ans en tant que designer junior, idéalement sur le jersey et/ou le flou.

Vous avez également :

Contexte du recrutement

Dans un contexte de développement et de transformation continue, Theodo France doit poursuivre sa croissance, renforcer son excellence opérationnelle et assurer l’alignement entre ses ambitions stratégiques et leur mise en œuvre au quotidien.

En devenant Chief of Staff, tu seras au cœur des décisions et des enjeux de développement de Theodo France.

Tu développeras une compréhension approfondie du fonctionnement d’une entreprise technologique, de la définition de sa stratégie à son exécution opérationnelle. Tu travailleras directement avec la direction sur des problématiques variées, avec un niveau d’exposition élevé et une forte autonomie.

As a Account Executive at INFINIT, you will own revenue generation within our key account level customer segment, focusing on winning high-value, strategic new-business opportunities. You will engage with senior stakeholders, navigate complex sales cycles, and create tailored value propositions that showcase how INFINIT’s AI-driven fintech platform transforms business operations.
 
We are looking for a high-performing hunter with a strong track record of closing larger deals, managing multi-stakeholder relationships, and driving high-impact commercial outcomes.

🚲Derrière chaque piste cyclable pérennisée, chaque site naturel préservé, il y a une décision. Et derrière cette décision, il y a nos données.

Chez Eco-Compteur, nous aidons les villes et les gestionnaires d’espaces naturels à décider sur des faits, pas à l’intuition.

Nos capteurs connectés mesurent la fréquentation piétons et cyclistes, en ville comme en pleine nature, et nos logiciels transforment ces données en indicateurs concrets : impact d’un aménagement, évolution de la pratique, effet des saisons. Parce que compter, c’est bien, mais donner du sens aux chiffres, c’est encore mieux !

🌍 Pionniers et leader mondial d’un métier que nous avons créé il y a plus de 20 ans, nous sommes basés en Bretagne, avec des filiales sur quatre continents et des solutions présentes dans plus de 55 pays.

Envie que vos compétences aient un impact concret ? Nous recherchons notre prochain·e :

Stage de fin d’études · 6 mois · Lannion (22)

Nous préparons un nouveau banc de test capable de piloter une dizaine de produits différents. Chaque produit sera relié à une carte de pilotage qui gère ses interfaces, son alimentation et la mesure de sa consommation. Un poste central dialogue ensuite avec chacune de ces cartes pour dérouler les tests et scénarios attendus.

Le défi : router les bons bus vers le bon produit selon le test en cours (USB, UART, I2C, JTAG, …), et pouvoir déconnecter physiquement les équipements pour mesurer la consommation sans perturbation.

Tu utiliseras Claude (IA) au quotidien pour t’aider dans la conception, le développement et la documentation.

– Recenser les besoins de test des produits (interfaces, séquences, mesures) et définir l’architecture du banc

– Concevoir la carte de pilotage (schéma, routage, mise au point) : commutation des bus, déconnexion physique des équipements, alimentation et mesure de consommation (précision, calibration, asservissement)

– Développer son firmware et le protocole de communication avec le poste central

– Développer le logiciel de supervision qui pilote chaque carte et déroule les scénarios de test

– Intégrer le banc à notre chaîne CI/CD (Jenkins, Git) pour lancer les tests automatiquement

– Valider le banc sur les produits, documenter et le mettre en service

Le poste est basé à Lannion, Bretagne, au sein d’une technopole à taille humaine d’envergure mondiale (1er centre R&D Orange Labs en France et 2ème site Nokia français). Les loisirs, nautiques notamment, sont particulièrement accessibles par la localisation à 5 km de la Côte de Granit Rose

Ce que l’on te met à disposition :

  • Des outils performants qui permettront d’exprimer pleinement tes talents

  • Une équipe de passionnés qui travaillera à tes côtés


👉Et si c’était toi ?

– Bac+5, école d’ingénieur ou master en électronique / systèmes embarqués

– Électronique numérique : bus UART, I2C, JTAG, conception de cartes

– Firmware embarqué en C sur microcontrôleur

– Bases en mesure de courant, alimentation et asservissement

– Python pour la supervision et l’automatisation des tests, Git, CI/CD (Jenkins)

– Curieux(se), autonome, rigoureux(se), à l’aise en laboratoire

L’entreprise et le projet te plaisent ?

« il ne faut jamais remettre au lendemain ce qu'on peut faire le jour-même » : Tu n’es pas arrivé.e jusqu’ici pour postuler « plus tard » ! C’est rapide, ça prend 2 minutes (et c’est vrai !)

rawCandidates.descriptionText:
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Sujet de stage

Doctrine développe des workflows dédiés aux professionnels du droit pour accélérer et améliorer la gestion de leurs dossiers. Parmi eux, Jobexit accompagne les avocats et juristes en droit social dans la simulation de ruptures du contrat de travail, notamment en calculant les indemnités de départ, les indemnités en cas de contentieux, le calendrier de sortie et les allocations chômage.

Dans un litige, un salarié peut demander plusieurs choses à la fois : des salaires impayés, une indemnité de licenciement, des dommages et intérêts, etc. L'objectif du stage est de permettre à l'utilisateur de saisir et d'organiser toutes ces demandes dans l'application, pour mieux estimer les montants en jeu, préparer la négociation avec la partie adverse et générer automatiquement le récapitulatif final destiné au juge. Ceci peut inclure :

  • Concevoir une interface pour ajouter, modifier et réordonner les demandes d'un dossier, chacune avec son montant, son unité de calcul et son ordre
  • Modéliser les dépendances entre demandes (une demande qui ne s'applique que si une autre est refusée par exemple)
  • Calculer et afficher les montants (du coût pour l’employeur au net empoché par le salarié), pour aider l'utilisateur à évaluer les risques
  • Générer automatiquement un document de synthèse clair et structuré, prêt à être intégré dans les conclusions écrites de l'avocat
  • Et d'autres fonctionnalités !

Le ou la stagiaire participera à la compréhension du besoin utilisateur autour de ces outils (en collaboration avec les équipes produit et les juristes) et à la définition des solutions techniques (en collaboration avec les équipes techniques). Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Jobexit et participera également au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs fullstack de l’entreprise).

 


Les à-côtés du poste 👁️
Le ou la stagiaire participera comme tous les ingénieurs à son chapter (réuni 2 fois par mois) dont le but est de :
  • Partager des connaissances entre ses membres (amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques)
  • Proposer des améliorations (nouveaux outils et processus)
  • Aider ses membres en fonction de leurs besoins

    • Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝

    • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert.
    • Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides.
    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.
    • Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc.

    Nos valeurs 🤝

    Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

    • Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur.
    • Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership.
    • Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser.
    • Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques.
     

    Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️

    🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine.

    🌴 Une politique de congés flexibles

    🌱 Des opportunités concrètes de mobilité interne

    🏄‍♂️ Des évènements collectifs réguliers

    📚 Un vrai accent sur la formation individuelle et collective, avec un budget annuel de 750€ pour toute formation en lien avec ton poste - et des formations en équipe ou pour toute l'entreprise

    🏋️‍♀️ Un abonnement Gymlib pour les activités sportives et bien-être

    🧘 Un accès gratuit à la plateforme d'accompagnement à la santé mentale Moka.care et un accompagnement individuel allant jusqu’à 6 séances par an

    👩‍⚕️ Une assurance santé avec Alan

    🍱 🚲 Une carte Swile pour tes tickets restaurants et ton forfait mobilité durable (66,60 euros par mois)

    💡 Des réductions et avantages négociés grâce à notre CSE via la plateforme Happypal

    🍏 Un équipement de travail neuf chez Apple

     

    Notre processus de recrutement 🚀

    • Un premier échange de 30 min avec l’un.e de nos Talent Acquisition Manager pour bien comprendre ton projet professionnel et te présenter ce qu'on construit chez Doctrine
    • Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions.
    • Un ou deux tests techniques pour évaluer concrètement tes compétences
    • Une venue dans nos bureaux pour : un déjeuner avec 3 personnes de différents départements chez Doctrine, pour te donner un aperçu de tes futur.e.s collègues ; un échange sur les valeurs de l’entreprise pour te partager notre vision, et une rencontre avec notre CEO, Guillaume.
    (si nécessaire le processus pourra être adapté pour répondre à tes contraintes personnelles et professionnelles)
     
     
    Mesdames, autorisez-vous à candidater !
    Certaines études scientifiques montrent qu'en particulier les femmes ont moins tendance à postuler à une offre d'emploi quand elles n'ont pas toutes les qualifications. Si cela peut vous rassurer, sachez que cette fiche de poste est indicative donc prenez la comme telle : c'est un guide, ni plus ni moins.
    Si Doctrine vous intéresse, sachez que nous aurons plaisir à recevoir votre candidature !
     
    Diversité & inclusion
    Toutes nos offres sont ouvertes aux personnes en situation de handicap, n'hésitez pas a nous en parler lors du process de recrutement.

rawCandidates.title: Software Engineer - Dynamics
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Software Engineer to join the Dynamics team within Ground Platform. Dynamics computes the timeline of what every spacecraft in our fleet can do and when (contacts with ground stations, links, accesses, unavailability windows) and turns it into schedules: which satellite talks to which ground station, when, and in which order of priority.

As our fleet grows, these services need to handle more data, more queries, and harder allocation problems. You’ll bring strong backend engineering to that challenge: making our APIs fast, our databases scale, and our contact allocation and scheduling smarter. No astrodynamics background is needed; you’ll work alongside flight dynamics engineers who bring that expertise.

If you enjoy hard performance problems and optimization with real-world constraints, we’d love to hear from you.


About this role:
  • Build and optimize our scheduling capabilities: model constraints and objectives, design algorithms and solver-based approaches that produce feasible, high-quality schedules across a growing fleet, and replan quickly when things change
  • Evolve contact allocation (Contact Allocation Framework) to share ground station capacity across satellites and missions
  • Improve the performance of our backend services and APIs: profile, find bottlenecks and cut latency for the timeline and scheduling services that operators and other teams rely on
  • Design and evolve our data layer for large, fast-growing time-based datasets: data modeling, partitioning, indexing, query optimization and retention
  • Shape the architecture of Dynamics services for low latency and scale, in step with the rest of Ground Platform
  • Collaborate with flight dynamics engineers, Mission Platform (Execution & Insights) and satellite operators to turn their needs into reliable, performant software
  • Have the opportunity to take part in spacecraft operations through SatDevOps rotations, occasionally helping investigate anomalies

    • Must Haves:
  • Solid backend software development experience, in Python
  • Strong algorithmic foundations for scheduling and optimization problems: modeling constraints and objectives, heuristics, and knowing when to reach for a solver
  • Proven track record improving the performance of APIs or backend services (profiling, caching, concurrency, load testing)
  • Strong relational database skills, ideally PostgreSQL: data modeling, indexing, partitioning, reading query plans
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

    • Nice to Haves:
  • Experience with constraint programming or operations research (e.g. OR-Tools / CP-SAT, MILP solvers), or with scheduling and allocation problems
  • Django and GraphQL (Graphene)
  • Time-series or geospatial data at scale (e.g. TimescaleDB, PostGIS)
  • Kubernetes and observability tooling (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana)
  • Interest in space (astrodynamics knowledge not required)

    • Some of Our Awesome Benefits:
  • Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable
    •  *Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions.  We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes.

    Who We Are

    Loft: Space Made Simple. 

    Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

    We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

    With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

    As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

Lucis is a preventive health app. A complete blood check-up lets members read a wide range of biomarkers, then get a personalised action plan to improve their health, performance and recovery.

Lucis is the National Partner of HYROX France for the 2026-2027 season and title partner of HYROX Toulouse, as part of a three-year partnership. Around it we run an athletes team, a network of partner HYROX gyms, and community events like trainings and shakeout runs.

rawCandidates.descriptionText:
Meet Arago and the Aragonians

Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors.

Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs.

Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles:

  1. Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to.

  2. High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time.

  3. One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie.

Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders.

What you’ll do

As a Drivers & Virtualization Engineer, you will own the host-facing software boundary of Arago’s accelerator. Your mission is to ensure our hardware is accessible, secure, and performant across diverse environments—ranging from bare-metal deployments to complex virtualized and multi-device cloud infrastructures. You will focus on building robust kernel-level interfaces where correctness, isolation, and long-term operational safety are paramount.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

  • Deep knowledge of OS internals, particularly kernel memory management and I/O paths.

  • Strong understanding of memory safety requirements in kernel space.

  • Proven hands-on experience in Linux kernel driver development and kernel modules.

  • Solid understanding of virtualization fundamentals (KVM, hypervisors).

  • Practical experience with emulation frameworks, specifically QEMU internals or custom device models.

  • Familiarity with hardware-level protocols: PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and IOMMU.

  • Language: English at a proficient level. French is a plus.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain high-performance Linux kernel drivers for Arago’s proprietary accelerator.

  • Implement communication protocols and virtual device interfaces to bridge hardware and software.

  • Manage low-level hardware interactions including PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and interrupt handling.

  • Enable seamless virtualized access to accelerators using QEMU and KVM.

  • Design and implement robust device sharing, passthrough, and isolation mechanisms.

  • Ensure the security of accelerator operations through strict memory protection and resource isolation.

  • Debug complex failures that span the entire stack: from hardware and kernel to hypervisor and guest OS.

  • Support the scaling of our architecture from single-device setups to large-scale multi-device deployments.

Pay and benefits

  • Competitive cash compensation, with final package based on location, experience, and the pay of team members in similar positions.

  • Meaningful stock option plan offered at the earliest stage of the company (included in the majority of full time offers).

  • Relocation bonus and coverage of moving expenses for relocation within 20 minutes of the company’s location.

  • Healthcare coverage (including family-friendly options), pension contributions, professional development support, and 25 days of PTO, in addition to public holidays.

  • Ownership of a key technical domain, with significant vertical and/or horizontal growth opportunities, based on performance and individual drive.

  • Reimbursement of 50% of the public transport subscription fee.

  • A high-paced, multicultural (with 10 nationalities), and engineering-led environment.

Our Hiring Process: Your Journey to Arago

  • Screening Call : Get to know you beyond your CV.

  • Technical meeting : Deep dive into your past projects and technical achievements.

  • CEO Interview : Assess the fit with the team’s culture and long-term vision.

  • Reference Calls: Mandatory calls with your former managers to validate strengths, weaknesses, and work style.

  • Technical Assessment: Take-home technical assignment crafted to the role you’re applying for.

  • Final Interview : Discuss your technical assignment and address any remaining questions with team members.

rawCandidates.title: Product Frontend Engineer
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where this is going

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.

Why this role exists

Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening.

How we work

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own

Everything on the screen:

  • The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.
  • The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.
  • The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.
  • Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.
  • The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins.

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Sierra was co-founded by Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor who first met while working together at Google over 20 years ago. Bret currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Open AI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce and CTO of Facebook. Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs.

What you'll do

As an Agent Strategist, you own how Sierra's AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. You transform a customer's thorniest, highest-stakes problems into agents that measurably move their business.

  • Own the Agent Development Life Cycle. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it's the best version of itself in the real world. You'll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

  • Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers' executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

  • Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.

Example projects

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

  • Scope and launch a subscription-retention agent for a large telecommunications or media company that consistently outperforms human agents at saving at-risk customers.

  • Stand up an agent for a commerce customer that troubleshoots a broken device end-to-end and personalizes product recommendations in the same conversation.

  • Redesign the conversation flows for a financial services agent so it can handle complex, regulated interactions — and convert a pilot into a multi-team production deployment. See our financial services blog for examples.

  • Partner with product on a net-new capability — a new agent architecture or self-service tooling — using a live customer as the design partner.

  • Define the evaluation and quality bar for a new agent, then use those metrics to drive a measurable lift in outcome week over week.

What you'll bring

  • Customer obsession. Genuine energy being in front of customers — understanding their business and needs, thriving in complex organizations, and building trusted relationships.

  • Communication. Clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strategic problem-solving in ambiguity. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to break down complex problems, spot risks early, and adapt as things change fast.

  • Technical aptitude. Comfortable engaging directly with technical concepts - reading API documentation, understanding data models and system architecture, and following engineering tradeoffs in a design discussion.

  • Ownership and delivery. A track record of running multiple complex, high-visibility projects at once and driving them to outcomes.

Even better...

  • Experience building or deploying AI/LLM agents in production — hands-on with the tools behind them (eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering) — working closely with technical counterparts.

  • You've been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience — and/or an MBA or comparable experience at the intersection of technology and business.

Our values

  • Trust: We do the right thing, even when no one is looking, and even when it’s hard. When we screw up, we take accountability, fully and completely. We act in such a way that if all of our actions were completely visible to our customers, we would be proud.

  • Customer Obsession: Our entire business is designed to ensure every agent built on Sierra succeeds, and that we are accountable to our customers and their success. We do whatever it takes to make our customers successful, and we go the extra mile in how we show up as a partner with unreasonable hospitality.

  • Craftsmanship: A great company is the aggregation of thousands of things done well. As they say, “how you do anything is how you do everything”. Most important is craftsmanship in building agents that are so great that people thank them at the end of a call. That’s the standard.

  • Intensity: We operate with urgency, and we want to win. We are never complacent. We fight to win every deal, big or small, using the full force of the company. And when we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

  • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We work hard, and turn on the afterburners when needed. But we pick up our parents at the airport when they’re visiting from out of town. We go to our kids’ events. And we show up for one another, in moments of celebration and hardship.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

  • Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

  • Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

  • Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region and employment type, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. rawCandidates.descriptionText:
About Invisix

Semiconductor manufacturers can't build what they can't measure. Invisix Measuring Systems is a fast-growing scale-up in the high-tech industry, developing next-generation metrology solutions for the semiconductor sector. We work at the intersection of optics, software, and data.

We're a small team, but the depth of knowledge inside Invisix is anything but small. Our culture is professional and fast-paced, with short communication lines and a strong sense of shared purpose. Everyone here is committed, and everyone knows their work directly contributes to something bigger.

The Role

We're looking for a System Architect to decide what our metrology equipment is and why it's built that way: concept choices, system decomposition, budget allocations and the technology roadmap amongst others.

Reporting to our CTO, you look two to five years ahead and beyond, and shape our product line across several generations, so that what we build today still makes sense for our customers tomorrow. You work with our customers' technology roadmaps, marketing, the heads of R&D, our function architects and customer support, and you lead through persuasion rather than formal authority. Our system engineer builds on your concept and makes the current program work to spec. The role includes occasional travel to customers in Asia, the US and Europe.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the system architecture of our metrology product line, looking two to five years ahead and beyond, across several product generations

  • Make and justify the key concept choices, weighing physics, performance, cost and risk

  • Decompose the system into modules and interfaces, and allocate the key budgets, such as throughput, cost of goods, availability and performance

Why Protolabs? 
We are the leaders in digital manufacturing.  We hire doers, makers, and creative thinkers who tackle our roles with an entrepreneurial spirit.  Our culture is centered around meaningful work that brings new and innovative products to market at unprecedented speeds.  We are a diverse team that comes from all walks of life and take pride in our team who is smart, genuine, humble, and passionate about what we do.  It’s our people who fuel our creativity and make our culture feel like home. 

Join our team as a

Senior Machine Learning Engineer - AI Technical Lead!

This is a hybrid role, and we are currently considering candidates based in the Netherlands.
 
Protolabs is a digital manufacturing company that turns CAD files and technical drawings into physical parts  fast and at scale. Our AI team builds systems that empower workflows in digital manufacturing such as finding similar parts, geometry understanding, and automated routing of work to the right expert.
 
We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to act as Technical Lead for our horizontal innovation work, the foundational technical building blocks that serve multiple use cases across the value chain.

The work is distinct in that the technology often comes first and the use case follows: this is true innovation, where you prove a capability is possible and then drive it into business value. You will be the single technical point of contact for these initiatives, driving core development of transformative capabilities. You will observe the market, bring new innovations into the organization, and partner across engineering and business teams to turn technology into measurable impact — mentoring and influencing engineers inside and outside your own team without formal authority.

What You Will Do:
Technical leadership & core development
  • Drive core development of transformative capabilities.
  • Take over full technical ownership as the primary technical contact for product management, engineering management, and partner teams on the delivery and roadmap of these initiatives.
  • Create, maintain, and review the technical roadmap together with product and engineering management.
  • Provide architectural guidance for ML systems on inference, agentic approaches and hybrid AI systems; industrialize and maintain proven-value use cases.
    • Technical implementation across a broad range of AI use cases

    • Cross-organisation delivery & architecture
  • Partner with other engineering teams to deliver business impact through integrating new technologies and new solutions.
  • Draft, share, and align architectural designs for each building block across the organisation, obtaining sign-off from affected teams before integration starts; bring designs to architecture board review.
    • Platform & environment
  • Contribute to foundational environments for (Gen)AI experimentation, model development, evaluation, and deployment.
  • Collaborate with global platform counterparts to implement MLOps, CI/CD, data pipelines, and observability.
  • Advocate for reusable components, shared libraries, and internal tooling to accelerate usecase delivery.
    • Mentoring & influencing
  • Mentor and coach engineers across the organisation — inside and outside your own team— through PR reviews, work scoping, design reviews, and documentation reviews.
  • Proactively surface in-team and cross-team barriers to leadership as they arise, with suggestions on how to resolve them.
  • Identify needs and tech-stack gaps blocking engineers from delivering, and raise them for prioritization.

    • What You Bring:
    Technical
  • 7+ years of hands-on AI/ML engineering experience, with strong depth in machine learning and deep learning — modeling, data pipelines, evaluation, and shipping models to production using state-of-the-art frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras, scikit-learn, XGBoost).

Hoofd Servicemonteur
Als Hoofd Servicemonteur ben jij het technische boegbeeld van onze serviceafdeling. Waar een reguliere servicemonteur de standaard onderhoudsbeurten en reparaties uitvoert, kom jij in beeld bij de complexe uitdagingen. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het optimaal laten draaien van onze vloot aan warmtepompen door heel Nederland. Je coacht je collega-monteurs in het veld en bent de schakel tussen de praktijk en ons engineering-team.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Specialistische Service: Je lost complexe, niet-alledaagse storingen op die een diepgaande analyse vereisen (zowel mechanisch, thermodynamisch als softwarematig).

  • Technisch Coach: Je bent de achterwacht (2e lijns support) voor je collega-servicemonteurs. Als zij vastlopen in het veld, bellen ze jou voor technisch advies of kom je ter plaatse ondersteunen.

  • Kwaliteitsbewaking: Je analyseert servicerapporten, signaleert terugkerende problemen en doet verbetervoorstellen om de betrouwbaarheid van onze systemen te verhogen.

  • Customer Excellence: Je zorgt dat de servicebeleving voor onze klanten van topniveau is en traint je team in hoe zij klanten het beste kunnen adviseren over hun warmtepompsysteem.

  • Feedbackloop: Je koppelt bevindingen uit het veld direct terug aan de productontwikkelaars in Den Haag om de volgende generatie warmtepompen nóg beter te maken.

Wie zoeken wij?

  • De Expert: Je hebt uitgebreide ervaring in het servicen van CV-installaties, koeltechniek of warmtepompen. Je leest technische schema’s als een krant.

  • Analytisch: Je vindt het leuk om diep in de data en de techniek te duiken om de oorzaak van een probleem te vinden.

  • Mentor-rol: Je krijgt er energie van om jouw kennis over te dragen aan minder ervaren collega's en hen te helpen groeien.

  • Opleiding & Certificering: Een afgeronde MBO-4 opleiding (Installatietechniek/Elektrotechniek).

  • Communicatie: Je kunt complexe techniek simpel uitleggen aan zowel een klant als aan een meer junior collega.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Sleutelpositie: Een verantwoordelijke baan in de frontlinie van de energietransitie bij een ambitieuze scale-up.

  • Ontwikkeling: Mogelijkheid om door te groeien naar Field Lead of Technisch Specialist binnen de R&D afdeling.

  • Topmateriaal: Een luxe servicebus met de modernste meetinstrumenten en gereedschap.

  • Cultuur: Werken bij een innovatieve werkgever met veel vrijheid, korte lijnen en een jong, gedreven team.

  • Arbeidsvoorwaarden: Een salaris dat recht doet aan jouw expertise en senioriteit (€3500-€5000), goede pensioenregeling en 38 vakantiedagen.

Over DeWarmte

Wij geloven dat verduurzaming makkelijker én slimmer kan. Met onze warmtepompen bieden we een innovatieve oplossing voor de Nederlandse huishoudens. Ons serviceteam is cruciaal voor het vertrouwen van de klant in deze nieuwe techniek.

Compensation: €3.5K – €5K per month

Samen met de teamleider zorg je voor een gezonde werkvoorraad en verdere groei van het team.

Dit ben jij bij Movares

Je bent een ondernemende adviseur die inhoudelijke deskundigheid verbindt met commercieel inzicht. Je legt gemakkelijk nieuwe contacten en weet vertrouwen op te bouwen bij opdrachtgevers en partners. Veel ontwikkelmogelijkheden

Ontwikkel een loopbaan die past bij jouw talenten en ambities. Kies jouw eigen pad:

  • leren door te doen, samen met ervaren collega's en met gebruik van een breed aanbod aan ontwikkelmogelijkheden;

Samen groeien

Deel mee in de waarde die we samen creëren en de groei van onze organisatie. Samen voor succes:

De komende jaren wil het team zijn marktpositie en maatschappelijke impact verder vergroten. Jij helpt daarbij door inhoudelijke expertise te verbinden met nieuwe klantvragen en commerciële kansen. rawCandidates.title: Senior SEO & GEO Manager
rawCandidates.descriptionText:
Who we are

We believe travel can create Citizens of the World. When people cross Europe slowly, by train, they come back more curious, more open and better able to understand people unlike themselves.

 

With colleagues from more than 50 countries, our diversity sparks curiosity, insight and a culture of openness, which is essential to understanding our travellers and one another.

 

Three values connect everyone at Interrail: we lead with our purpose, we own our impact, and we choose for growth.

 

We work in a hybrid way, from our office in Utrecht and our homes across the Netherlands.

 

Who we’re looking for

Someone who can shape how travellers discover Interrail, whether they’re typing into a search engine or asking an AI assistant to plan their trip. Exploring Europe by rail is one of the most transformative ways to travel, and there’s a big, untapped opportunity to make it even easier. With SEO and GEO, you’ll help travellers get inspired, plan and book their next rail adventure with an Interrail Pass in fewer steps.

 

Also, it’s good to know that the team has agreed to meet in the office every Tuesday and Thursday, so you’ll be expected to be in the office on these days to work side by side with your colleagues.

 

What you’ll be doing

You’ll be joining the Growth team (in a nutshell: the people who turn traveller curiosity into journeys booked), reporting to our E-Commerce Lead.

 

You’ll own the end-to-end SEO and GEO strategy, so that Interrail is found, cited and recommended wherever travellers research rail travel in Europe. Working across content, product, engineering and PR/brand, you’ll turn search and AI visibility insight into meaningful, measurable growth.

 

Strategy and leadership

  • Own and scale a unified SEO and GEO strategy and roadmap, aligned to commercial goals across our priority markets.

  • Prioritise investment across markets and languages based on search demand, commercial opportunity and local traveller needs.

  • Be our internal expert on how AI is changing travel discovery, embedding SEO and GEO thinking across marketing, content, PR/brand and product.

  • Partner with engineering, content and product to get the right work prioritised and shipped.

Technical SEO and architecture

  • Own technical SEO for our large, complex site and set the technical roadmap with product and content.

  • Lead our SEO architecture: hreflang at scale, domain and subfolder strategy, and localisation quality across languages.

  • Make sure search engines and AI systems can access and understand the site, with the right structured data and clear, consistent information on passes, pricing and eligibility.

  • Own our crawler access policy for AI bots together with legal and engineering, balancing visibility against content protection.

GEO

  • Own our GEO strategy and roadmap: how we earn mentions, citations and recommendations across markets and languages.

  • Build our GEO measurement framework, tracking brand presence, citation share, share of voice against competitors and sentiment.

  • Spot recurring inaccuracies in AI-generated answers, fix them at the source with the relevant teams and track whether accuracy improves.

  • Partner with PR, partnerships and social to strengthen the off-site signals AI models rely on, from trusted travel publications to community presence and review platforms.

  • Measure and attribute AI-referred traffic and conversions, and run structured tests to build repeatable GEO playbooks.

  • Assess emerging opportunities, such as AI agents that plan and book travel, and advise on what Interrail needs to be ready.

Content and topical authority

  • Shape content strategy and topical authority across destinations, routes, guides and inspiration, balancing discovery with pass and booking intent.

  • Make sure our content performs in both search results and AI answers, with clear factual structure and original rail expertise worth citing.

  • Be the SEO and GEO advisor to the content team, building a shared roadmap that connects visibility opportunity to editorial output.

  • Set and govern content quality standards (briefs, structure, internal linking, E-E-A-T) and upskill the team in SEO and GEO best practice.

  • Identify gaps, cannibalisation and refresh opportunities, and advise on what to create, update, consolidate or retire.

Measurement and reporting

  • Forecast organic and AI-driven performance, set KPIs across both, and report clearly to senior stakeholders.

What success looks like

  • Non-brand searches make up a growing share of organic traffic and revenue across our priority markets.

  • A GEO measurement framework is live, and our citation share and share of voice in AI answers are improving against key competitors.

  • The SEO and GEO roadmap is agreed with product, engineering and content and delivered as planned, including website and CMS changes that launch without loss of organic visibility.

  • Recurring inaccuracies about passes, pricing and eligibility in AI answers are identified, fixed at the source and measurably reduced.

What we’re looking for

Here’s what will help you in this role. If you don’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you.

 

In terms of your experience and skills:

  • Demonstrated experience leading SEO strategy across content and technical, ideally in travel, e-commerce or a large content or marketplace environment.

  • Hands-on GEO experience, with examples of your approach, results, measurement limitations and the decisions that followed.

  • A working understanding of how AI search experiences select and cite sources, and how that differs from traditional ranking.

  • A strong track record in international and multilingual SEO at scale.

  • A solid technical foundation, including structured data, and the ability to influence engineering roadmaps.

  • Outstanding cross-functional collaboration: you align teams around a shared roadmap and take initiatives from idea to launch without direct authority, reviewing results together and applying the learnings.

  • A data-driven, commercial mindset: comfortable forecasting, sizing opportunity, attributing impact in a maturing channel and presenting to leadership.

  • A test-and-learn mindset, comfortable building new capabilities in a fast-changing environment.

  • Experience partnering closely with content, editorial, PR or brand teams.

  • Fluency with the core toolset: Google Search Console, GA4, an SEO platform such as Semrush or Ahrefs, a crawler such as Screaming Frog, log-analysis tools and GEO tracking tools.

  • Fluent English; another European language, ideally German, French, Italian or Spanish, is beneficial to have.

Our offer

  • A hybrid way of working, with some days each week in our Utrecht office and the rest from home.
